newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil default rates seen steady in H1 1997.
newsitem.headline: Brazil default rates seen steady in H1 1997.

text.p: Debt defaults and bankruptcy filings in Brazil are likely to remain steady or post a slight drop in the first half of 1997, the Centralized Bank Services (Serasa) said.
"Debt default levels, which are still too high, may remain steady in the first half next year or drop a little bit," Serasa president Elcio De Lucca told reporters.

Serasa, a private data bank service for banks, said its forecast was based on the following reasons: unemployment and salaries were likely to remain steady next year; consumers would remain highly indebted making it hard for them to make new purchases; and interest rates would remain high.

Lucca said the number of debt relief filings dropped 62 percent to 764 in the first eleven months of the year over the same period in 1995, noting that the commercial sector accounted for 53.2 percent of all filings.
The number of legal complaints issued against unpaid debts fell 16.4 percent to 7.1 million between January and November 1996, he added.
Debt defaults fell this year due to the lengthening of debt maturity periods coupled with a gradual drop in interest rates and an increase in liquidity, Lucca said.
